clue.text: Out of action, having marched with boots in bad shape

indicators.note: something in bad shape is knocked out of form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier is out of action after marching in ill-fitting boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bad shape' rearranges MARCHED and BOOTS together; 'with' only links. HORS DE COMBAT is French for disabled in battle, used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means unable to fight, disabled or sidelined, as a wounded soldier is.

clue.text: Hard American group to manage carefully

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A tough American band needs careful management.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them sparingly and with care.

clue.text: Voraciously devour bird

explanation.surface: Someone gobbles up a bird greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To raven (also ravin) is an old verb for eating ravenously; the crow-family bird is the second sense.

clue.text: Awfully dirty room? It's for the rest of the pupils

definitions.text: It's for the rest of the pupils

indicators.note: awfully suggests the words are in a terrible mess, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A filthy room turns out to be where the schoolchildren sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' means sleep, not the remainder of the pupils: a boarding-school bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared sleeping room at a boarding school is where pupils go to rest at night.

clue.text: Slightly damage computer component

explanation.surface: A small knock damages a computer part.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick an edge is the verb sense; a silicon integrated circuit is the noun sense.

clue.text: Where a soldier was loved, and embraced by Asian

indicators.note: embraced by means the word and is held inside the word for an Asian

parts.note: a Malay is a person from the Malay peninsula, an Asian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier's romance with an Asian woman who hugged him.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'Mandalay' tells of a British soldier remembering the Burmese girl who loved him there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burmese city is the setting of Kipling's ballad about a soldier and his sweetheart.

clue.text: Religious leader's article bishops turned to

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two bishops give BB

indicators.note: turned means the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious leader's newspaper article, which the bishops consulted.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a monastery is a religious superior.

clue.text: With musical certainty, I compose orchestral works

parts.note: con is Italian for with, as in the musical direction con brio
a cert is a racing certainty

explanation.surface: Confident in their musical gift, a composer writes for orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compose' is a link, meaning make up; it is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces for soloist and orchestra are concertos, plural in Italian form.

clue.text: Appropriate article, that is very penetrating

indicators.note: penetrating means the pieces for that is and very go inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A highly incisive newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriate as a verb means to take for oneself, i.e. to steal.

clue.text: Money that's particularly effective

explanation.surface: Cash that works especially well.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold coin once worth a pound is the money; a sovereign remedy is one supremely effective.

clue.text: Killer of president and army leader

explanation.surface: A presidential assassin who was also a military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth shot Lincoln; William Booth founded and led the Salvation Army.

clue.text: A free television service, so-called

parts.note: to untie is to free from bonds

explanation.surface: A no-charge broadcaster, as it is nicknamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the British nickname for the BBC, the UK public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately called by this family nickname in Britain.

clue.text: It's cheap, badly executed, and unoriginal work

indicators.note: badly executed suggests something botched, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tacky, poorly made knock-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' supplies the letters ITS; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is an imitative piece copying another's style.

clue.text: Two generations in family tree

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal
a son is the next generation down from the dam

explanation.surface: A family tree showing two generations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family tree' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'tree'; 'in family' tells you mother and son are related.
explanation.definitionFit: The plum tree bearing small dark fruit is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Soft shoe shuffle as comic turn's ending

indicators.note: shuffle means the letters of as and comic are mixed up
ending picks out the final letter of turn

explanation.surface: A comedian closes his act with a soft-shoe shuffle dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather slipper of Native American origin is a type of soft shoe.

clue.text: Talk about American lake

parts.note: ca. (circa) means about
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A discussion about an American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A causerie is an informal chat or a light conversational essay.

clue.text: A couple of words from Rome cover the present situation

definitions.text: A couple of words from Rome

explanation.surface: Latin phrases describing how things currently stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin two-word phrase means the existing state of affairs.

clue.text: Key person left small amount, something of little value

parts.note: an inch is a small distance
a pin is something worthless, as in not caring a pin

explanation.surface: A vital figure leaves a meagre, almost worthless legacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The most important member of a team is its central, indispensable figure.

clue.text: Novel bringing great fortune to James

parts.note: lucky means bringing good fortune
Jim is a pet form of James

explanation.surface: A book that makes a man named James rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucky Jim is Kingsley Amis's 1954 comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a famous comic campus novel.

clue.text: Goat's driver

parts.note: a goat stands for a lecherous man, and what drives him is his sex drive

explanation.surface: Whoever herds the goat along.
explanation.walkthrough: The goat as symbol of lust makes its 'driver' an urge, not a herdsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual desire is what drives a lustful person, a goat in old slang.

clue.text: Sailor freed initially on condition list of charges is produced

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
if means on condition that

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of freed

explanation.surface: A sailor is released provided a price list is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or duties.

clue.text: Result of sunning part of oneself recklessly?

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: What happens to the body when you sunbathe without care.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun exposure brings out small brown pigment spots on the skin.

clue.text: Cash one accountant found in plant

parts.note: brass is slang for money
I is the Roman numeral one
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Money and an accountant discovered at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' is the cabbage genus, not a factory; 'found in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage family genus covers kale, sprouts and other vegetables.

clue.text: Person who's succeeded splendidly

parts.note: s. is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
well means splendidly or excellently

explanation.surface: Someone who has done brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is an old slang term for a fashionable, upper-class man.

clue.text: Savoury dish he required for end of fast

indicators.note: required for the end of says the last letter of the word for fast is replaced

parts.note: quick means fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man needs a savoury dish to break his fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required for end of' swaps the K at the end of QUICK for HE; 'end of fast' looks like breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury open tart of egg custard is a classic savoury dish.

clue.text: Noisily root for food

explanation.surface: Loudly support your team, for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout support for is the verb; good cheer is an old word for food and drink.

clue.text: Saint installed by primate in part of church

indicators.note: installed by means the saint is put inside the word for primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A saint placed by an ape in a section of church.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Press are reportedly found in disreputable joint

indicators.note: found in means the letter goes inside the seedy bar word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club

indicators.note: reportedly means the word are is taken as it sounds, the letter R

parts.note: are sounds like the letter R

explanation.surface: Journalists are said to hang out in a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists, but it is the verb: to press on or urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to push or urge forward forcefully.

clue.text: Insignificant person wanting Dickensian hero to escape

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Great Expectations
a narrow squeak is a close escape

explanation.surface: A nobody wishing a Dickens hero to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipsqueak is a small, unimportant person.

clue.text: Torture undergone by learner in musical venue

indicators.note: torture twists the letters out of shape, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A learner suffers agonies in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torture' rearranges UNDERGONE, BY and L together. Glyndebourne is an English country-house opera festival in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a celebrated opera house and festival in southern England.
